note: Billionaire Life prototype. Every date and number below appears in at least one cited source. Situations and outcomes are summarized in our own words and simplified. Alternatives are generic choices for the game, not claims about what he considered.

person.name: Elon Musk
person.role: Founder and CEO of SpaceX; CEO of Tesla
person.bio: Co-founded Zip2, sold to Compaq in 1999, then co-founded PayPal, sold to eBay in 2002. Has run SpaceX since May 2002 and been Tesla's CEO since October 2008. Also founded Neuralink and The Boring Company. Degrees in physics and business from the University of Pennsylvania.

bioSource.title: SpaceX IPO prospectus (Form 424B4), directors and executive officers

decisions.title: Cash out, or go again?
decisions.situation: Zip2, the internet software company you co-founded in 1995, is being bought by Compaq. The deal, agreed in February 1999, pays about $307 million in cash. You have worked there as chairman, CEO and chief technology officer at different times.

options.label: Take the money and invest it safely
Start a new internet company right away
Stay on at Compaq and run Zip2 there

decisions.actual: In March 1999 he founded X.com and became its CEO. A year later, in March 2000, X.com merged with rival Confinity, and the combined company became PayPal.
decisions.outcome: He was PayPal's CEO from May to September 2000, then left that job but stayed on the board; in September 2001 he owned about 14.2% of the company. In July 2002 eBay agreed to buy PayPal in a stock deal valued at $1.5 billion.

sources.title: eBay to acquire PayPal (press release filed with the SEC)

decisions.title: Another web company, or rockets?
decisions.situation: You are no longer PayPal's CEO but still sit on its board with a large stake. You could build another internet business you already understand. The alternative is space: no private company has ever put a liquid-fuel rocket into orbit.

options.label: Become an investor in other people's startups

decisions.actual: Space Exploration Technologies (SpaceX) was incorporated on March 14, 2002, and he has been its CEO, chief technology officer and chairman since May 2002. Later that year, in October 2002, eBay completed its purchase of PayPal.
decisions.outcome: With Falcon 1 in 2008, SpaceX became the first private company to put a liquid-fuel rocket into orbit. As of March 31, 2026 it had flown about 650 orbital launches. In June 2026 it went public at $135 a share, a deal CNBC said valued it at $1.77 trillion.

sources.title: SpaceX raises $75 billion in record-setting IPO ahead of Nasdaq debut

decisions.title: Put more of your own money in?
decisions.situation: It is late 2008. You have chaired Tesla since April 2004, and in October 2008 you took over as its CEO just as volume production of the Roadster began. Earlier in the year you had already lent Tesla about $18 million. Now it is raising money again.

options.label: Stop here and let outside investors decide
Put millions more of your own money into Tesla
Look for a big carmaker to buy Tesla

decisions.actual: In the December 2008 bridge financing his trust lent Tesla about $20.4 million more. Counting the February 2008 notes and interest, about $41.0 million was later turned into Tesla preferred stock at a 60% discount to what other investors in that round paid.
decisions.outcome: Also in December 2008, NASA gave SpaceX a $1.6 billion contract for 12 space station cargo missions. Tesla took a $465 million US Department of Energy loan in January 2010 and went public in June 2010 at $17 a share.

sources.title: Commercial cargo: NASA's management of commercial orbital transportation services and ISS commercial resupply contracts (IG-13-016)

decisions.title: Speed up after 325,000 orders?
decisions.situation: Tesla has started taking deposits for Model 3, a mass-market car with a $35,000 base price. In the first week it received more than 325,000 reservations, about $14 billion in implied sales. You already have a plan to build 500,000 cars across all models, but it is years away.

options.label: Pull the 500,000-car plan two years forward
Close reservations until the factory is ready

decisions.actual: In May 2016 Tesla moved its 500,000-car build plan up two years to 2018. It said 2016 capital spending would be about 50% above its earlier $1.5 billion guidance and that it would likely need more money.
decisions.outcome: Model 3 deliveries began in July 2017, and Tesla said the production ramp was hard. In 2025 Tesla delivered 1,585,279 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, out of 1,636,129 in total.

sources.title: Tesla fourth quarter 2025 production, deliveries and deployments (Exhibit 99.1)

decisions.title: Fight in court, or buy Twitter after all?
decisions.situation: In April 2022 you agreed to buy Twitter for $54.20 a share in cash, about $44 billion and a 38% premium. On July 8 you sent notice that you were ending the deal. Twitter sued you in Delaware's Chancery Court, and a trial is coming.

options.label: Go to trial and try to walk away
Close the deal at the original price

decisions.actual: On October 3, 2022 his advisers told Twitter he would close on the original terms if the court paused the case. The purchase closed on October 27, 2022, and shareholders received $54.20 a share.
decisions.outcome: He renamed Twitter X and merged it into his AI company xAI in March 2025. In February 2026 SpaceX bought xAI in a deal CNBC said valued xAI at $250 billion. In March 2026 a San Francisco jury found two of his May 2022 tweets about the deal materially false or misleading, but found no scheme to defraud; his lawyers said they would appeal. As of that date, plaintiffs estimated damages of up to $2.6 billion.
